chunks: From him, from Al-Hajjal, from Aasim ibn Humayd, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'O group of those who became Muslims by their tongues but did not become Muslims by their hearts! Do not pursue the slips of the Muslims. For whoever pursues the slips of the Muslims, Allah will pursue his slip; and whoever Allah pursues his slip, He will expose him to shame.'
ai.seo_question: What is the consequence of exposing the faults of other Muslims according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In *Al-Kafi*, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this hadith to establish the principle of *satr* (concealing faults) as a core component of faith, distinguishing between outward conformity and inner sincerity. The warning against *tatabbu' al-'atharat* (scrutinizing slips) serves as a spiritual safeguard, ensuring that the critic does not become the one exposed by Allah on the Day of Judgment. This narration underscores the Shia emphasis on humility and avoiding the arrogance of judging others' hidden states.
